handbookNote: Nevada Commercial Driver's License Manual (AAMVA-authored base content copyright 2022, 'Modernized/2005 CDL Testing System', Version: July 2017 for Sections 1-10/12-13, with Section 11 'Vehicle Inspection Test' revised to AAMVA's newer itemized checklist format dated September 9, 2022, plus Nevada-specific front matter), published by the Nevada Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) -- fetched directly from https://dmv.nv.gov/pdfforms/dlbookcomm.pdf on 2026-08-22 (6.7MB PDF, full text extracted via pdftotext -layout to scratchpad/nv_cdl_research/nv_cdl_manual_full.txt, 9,853 lines, cross-checked against a pdftotext -raw extraction for any two-column table misalignment). Price matches this project's established CDL tier ($6.99). Exam mechanics: Nevada's manual, like several other AAMVA-base-manual states already built in this project (e.g. Kentucky, Louisiana, Alabama), does NOT disclose a specific number of knowledge-test items or a numeric passing score anywhere in the fetched text -- Section 1.1.1/1.1.2 describe which knowledge tests exist (general knowledge, passenger transport, air brakes, combination vehicles, hazardous materials, tank vehicle, doubles/triples, school bus) and that the skills test has three segments (vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, on-road driving, taken in that order with each segment passed before the next), but no item-count or per-test passing-score figure is stated for Nevada specifically. This is hedged rather than invented; the federally standardized minimum of 80 percent correct applies regardless (49 CFR 383.135(a)). Real, non-hedged Nevada-specific mechanics that ARE explicitly disclosed in the manual and were used directly in the question bank: a Commercial Learner Permit (CLP) is valid for a 180-day period and must be held at least 14 calendar days from initial issuance before the skills test may be taken; renewing a CLP a second time requires retaking all applicable knowledge tests, and no skills-test segments can be 'banked' across a CLP renewal; minimum age is 21 for interstate CMV operation (25 for an over-length combination vehicle of 70 feet), with 18-20 year olds eligible for intrastate-only operation excluding passengers-for-hire or placarded hazmat; original/renewal CDLs for holders under 65 expire 8 years from issuance, and for holders 65 and older expire 4 years from the holder's date of birth; the ten standardized restriction codes (E, K, L, M, N, O, P, V, X, Z) are described in full detail, as are the disqualification duration tables (BAC .04%+ -- 1 year first offense/3 years if hazmat-placarded/life for a second offense; 2-3 serious traffic violations in 3 years -- 60/120 days; out-of-service order violations -- 90 days/1 year/3 years for 1st/2nd/3rd within stated windows; railroad-crossing violations -- 60 days/120 days/1 year for 1st/2nd/3rd within 3 years). The CDL FEES table (front matter, roughly page vi-vii of the PDF) was found to be garbled/row-misaligned by the source PDF's two-column layout in both the -layout and -raw pdftotext extractions -- no specific dollar figures from that table were used in any question, per this project's standing policy of hedging rather than guessing at ambiguous extracted numbers. Nevada's three CDL vehicle classes are A (GCWR 26,001+ lbs with a towed unit over 10,000 lbs GVWR), B (single vehicle or such a vehicle towing a unit of 10,000 lbs GVWR or less, GVWR 26,001+ lbs), and C (does not meet A/B, but designed to carry 16+ passengers including the driver, or placarded for hazardous materials). Nevada's six CDL endorsements are T (Doubles/Triple Trailers), P (Passenger), N (Tank Vehicle), H (Hazardous Materials), X (combined Hazardous Materials and Tankers), and S (School Bus); only P, S, and N may be added to a CLP. Hazardous Materials endorsement applicants must pass a TSA fingerprint-based security threat assessment taking a minimum of 30 days, renewed at every CDL renewal, with a 90-day pre-expiration notice from DMV and up to a 30-day CDL suspension for lapsed authorization. Content-depth rationale: this manual uses the same AAMVA-authored base content as several other recently built CDL-track states in this project, organized into the same core sections -- Section 1 Introduction (CDL classes, endorsements/restrictions, disqualifications, other CDL rules, IRP/IFTA -- covered by 01_licensing.json together with the Nevada-specific front matter), Section 2 Driving Safely (the largest section at roughly 43 manual pages, split here into two buckets: 02_driving_safely_a covering subsections 2.1-2.16 -- vehicle inspection, basic control, shifting, seeing, communicating, speed/space management, seeing hazards, distracted/aggressive driving, night/fog/winter/hot-weather driving, railroad crossings, and mountain driving; 03_driving_safely_b covering subsections 2.17-2.23 -- driving emergencies, ABS, skid control/recovery, accident procedures, fires, alcohol/drugs, illness, and hazardous materials rules for all commercial drivers), Section 3 Transporting Cargo Safely (genuinely short in this manual at about 3 pages -- 04_cargo.json sized down accordingly, not padded), Section 4 Transporting Passengers Safely (also genuinely short at about 4 pages -- 05_passenger.json likewise sized down honestly), Section 5 Air Brakes (06_air_brakes.json), Section 6 Combination Vehicles (07_combination.json), Section 7 Doubles and Triples (short section -- 08_doubles_triples.json sized down; this section's actual text covers converter dollies, coupling/uncoupling procedures, inspection, and air brake checks specific to multiple trailers, and does not itself restate the rollover/rearward-amplification hazard content found in Section 6, so no such questions were fabricated for this bucket), Section 8 Tank Vehicles (09_tank.json), Section 9 Hazardous Materials (the second-largest section at roughly 22 pages, split into 10_hazmat_a.json covering 9.1-9.4 -- intent of the regulations, shipper/carrier/driver responsibilities, communication rules/shipping papers/placarding, and general loading requirements -- and 11_hazmat_b.json covering the remainder of 9.4 plus 9.5-9.8 -- bulk packaging, driving/parking rules, emergencies/fires, and the hazmat glossary), Section 10 School Buses (12_school_bus.json), Section 11 Vehicle Inspection Test (13_vehicle_inspection.json, drawing on Nevada's newer AAMVA itemized-checklist inspection format dated September 9, 2022, which yielded unusually rich, granular question material per discrete inspection item), and Sections 12-13 Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test and On-Road Driving (14_basic_control_onroad.json; Nevada's manual defines four basic-control exercises -- Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, and Reverse Offset Backing -- rather than the parallel-parking/alley-dock exercises seen in some other states' manuals, and no such exercises were invented for Nevada since they do not appear in this manual). Every question in this bank is grounded in a specific passage of the fetched official Nevada manual text cited in that question's source_note; none are invented, generic, or borrowed from another state's manual or numbers.
